bugs.title: [OVN] packet drops when provider network MTU exceeds tenant network MTU

blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is set, so the SRU needs to say this and the verification steps need to enable it. Also, the behaviour depends on OVN version support, and the comments don't show that this was checked for the Ubuntu OVN packages.

The original change introduced a regression (bug 2105383, wrong network_ids filter for redirect-type). The stable/2024.1 and 2024.2 backports squash the fix and the revert into one change. The Ubuntu SRU must include both together, and the squashed backport must be reviewed for the regression risk, because the Ubuntu cloud archive/package may not carry the combined patch.

Existing routers are not updated by the merged fix, so no maintenance or migration task sets gateway_mtu on them. Comment 25 had proposed this, but it was apparently not done. The SRU test plan and regression potential should account for upgraded deployments, where existing routers keep the problem until their ports are updated.

bugs.title: Unable to create instances after a new compute node is added due to Ceph key rotation

blockers.summary: The fix spans two charms. The nova-compute patch only sends the application name early, and an earlier attempt at that alone did not help. The ceph-mon side (ceph-charms PR 133/178) is only reported deployed to squid/stable, so older ceph-mon channels paired with the SRU'd nova-compute may not be fixed.

The ceph-mon fix is tracked only on GitHub/Launchpad comments with no linked review or backport status. The nova-compute charm's stable branches are fixed, but there is no evidence the combined fix was tested on yoga/zed-era deployments.

An earlier workaround test (moving send_application_name() to the top of ceph_joined()) did not resolve the race. The merged fix does essentially that, and no later comment confirms it works on its own or was verified on the stable branches.
The stable/ussuri backport was abandoned, and no explanation is given. The bug is tagged only for yoga and zed, and the older series remain unfixed.

There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

From: Hemanth Nakkina <email address hidden>
